Interface dispatch resolved by what flows, not by who implements
(TestExecDispatchFollowsTheFlow). One command hands dispatchlib.Drive a Quiet
runner; Loud, in a third package, implements the same interface and spawns. A
union over implementers would attribute Loud's spawn to the command; the call
graph must not, because no Loud value ever reaches Drive. The test's twin
rewrite passes Loud{} instead, and then the command must reach the spawn.

-- root.go --
package dispatchroot

import (
	"github.com/spf13/cobra"

	"example.com/fixture/dispatchlib"
	_ "example.com/fixture/dispatchloud"
)

// Quietly drives a runner that does nothing.
func Quietly() *cobra.Command {
	return &cobra.Command{
		Use: "quietly",
		RunE: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
			return dispatchlib.Drive(dispatchlib.Quiet{})
		},
	}
}

-- lib.go --
package dispatchlib

// Runner is dispatched through an interface, so which Go runs is a question of
// data flow.
type Runner interface{ Go() error }

type Quiet struct{}

func (Quiet) Go() error { return nil }

func Drive(r Runner) error { return r.Go() }

-- loud.go --
package dispatchloud

import "os/exec"

// Loud satisfies dispatchlib.Runner from another package and spawns.
type Loud struct{}

func (Loud) Go() error { return exec.Command("git", "gc").Run() }
